events.extended_summary: On November 20, as a one-day nationwide strike mobilized 1.5 million workers in Italy after similar strikes in France and Spain, youth protests were called across Europe. In France, thousands marched in Paris, as well as in Nantes and Lyon, and hundreds in Marseille, Toulouse, Dijon, and Rennes, where police banned the protest. A striking contradiction marked the day: as struggles explode across Europe, turnout in France was down after two months of struggle. There is growing social anger among workers and youth. But the union bureaucracies and opposition parties, like Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s La France insoumise (LFI), are not fighting for a revolutionary struggle of the working class. While millions have protested in France, the unions call isolated, widely spaced days of action, without mobilizing industries (like refineries, trucking, airports) that have seen militant strikes in recent years. events.extended_summary: Companies active in alternative energy and related technology have slammed the EU for plans to reduce the size of the European Competitiveness Fund as part of a broader 40 billion euro $44 billion budget cut. According to the group, featuring 75 companies and industry associations, the European Competitiveness Fund is vital for European businesses if they want to catch up with China and the United States in key industries, Reuters reported, citing a letter penned by the group, which includes energy heavyweights such as France’s EDF. At the end of last week, the president of the European Council, Antonio Costa, proposed a 40-billion-euro cut to the bloc’s budget for 2028 to 2034 from an earlier proposal made by the Irish EU presidency last month. However, compared to the European Commission’s original budget proposal, Costa’s version will shrink the budget by a much more substantial 180.6 billion, Reuters reported on Friday.
events.micro_summary: EU Green Energy Giants Slam 40 Billion Budget Cut.

events.extended_summary: Ukraine expects to produce hundreds of Neptune cruise missiles by the end of 2026, though fewer than 1,000, while annual production of UAV-290 Palianytsia cruise missiles has already exceeded 1,000 units. Production rates for both could increase if additional funding becomes available. The LUCH Design Bureau began developing the Neptune missile in 2010, with production funding arriving only in late 2020. The missile's first successful use in April 2022 marked a turning point for Ukraine's defense industry. Ukraine currently operates at least two Neptune versions: the Long Neptune (R-360L), with a claimed range up to 1,000 km and a 260 kg warhead, and the Thick Neptune (R-360). A variant informally called the Fat Neptune, unveiled in October 2025, features external fuel tanks extending its range to 400-600 km. The Palianytsia is a compact turbojet-powered cruise missile with a range of 650 km.
events.micro_summary: Ukraine plans to produce hundreds of Neptune cruise missiles by end of 2026 while Palianytsia output exceeds 1,000 annually.
events.summary: Ukraine expects to produce hundreds of Neptune cruise missiles by the end of 2026, fewer than 1,000, while annual production of Palianytsia missiles has already exceeded 1,000 units, with rates potentially rising with additional funding.

AVT units are atmospheric-vacuum distillation units where refining begins: crude oil is separated here into fractions, from which petrol, diesel, aviation fuel and fuel oil are then obtained. Without these units, the plant cannot process oil. The isomerisation unit raises the octane number of petrol, so without it the plant cannot produce high-quality fuel." events.extended_summary: Parastoo Ahmadi, a 29-year-old Iranian singer, and four members of her band and production team—Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia and Mohsen Lashkari—were each flogged 74 times on Monday at the third branch of the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom. The punishment followed their June conviction for offending public decency through a December 2024 YouTube livestream in which Ahmadi performed in a sleeveless dress without the mandatory hijab alongside male musicians. An appeals court rejected their appeal in September. In addition to the flogging, the five were banned for two years from audiovisual activities and from leaving Iran. Iranian law prohibits public performances by women and requires headscarves and modest clothing. Human rights activists and artists condemned the flogging as cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment violating international prohibitions on torture.
events.micro_summary: Parastoo Ahmadi and four team members were each flogged 74 times in Qom for a hijab-free concert.

The 73-year-old told French broadcaster BFM TV she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay. Pelicot made headlines across the world when she waived her right to anonymity in the trial of her then-husband Dominique, who was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her, as well as allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious. The publisher apologised, saying it would no longer print or promote the work after "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication". events.extended_summary: Ukrainian naval drones attacked the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi port, eastern Libya, over the weekend, leaving the 342-foot vessel largely submerged with only its bows visible. The attack, coordinated by Ukraine's SBU and armed forces, occurred more than 1,500 miles from the front lines in eastern Ukraine. President Volodymyr Zelensky described the operation as "an exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia's war." Seven Sea Baby drones loaded with explosives were launched from a mother ship during the strike. Simultaneously, the Russian cargo ship MV Angara was hit by a sea drone while transporting weapons, and the Sparta II had been hit in the Baltic the previous day. Russia condemned the attack as a dangerous escalation, while the UN mission in Libya expressed deep concern. The Merkury, commissioned in 2023 and capable of carrying KH-35 cruise missiles, was berthed in territory controlled by pro-Moscow Field Marshal Khalifa Haftar.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian sea drones sank Russia's corvette Merkury in Benghazi port, Libya.
events.summary: Ukrainian naval drones attacked and sank the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi, Libya, over the weekend, while simultaneously hitting the cargo ship MV Angara. President Zelensky called the strike, over 1,500 miles from the front lines, an exemplary operation.

events.extended_summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers arrested Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and his daughter Sofia Hernandez Mejia, both Mexican nationals, at Seattle-Tacoma Airport on Saturday morning while boarding an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles. ICE stated they were detained for allegedly overstaying visas and claimed Hernandez Mejia hurled hot coffee at officers, a federal felony. The Port of Seattle expressed outrage, while Alaska Airlines said it was not given appropriate notice and expressed concern. Videos showed officers in unmarked jackets dragging away one person as a woman screamed she had a work permit. The pair's lawyer said they were traveling to a family baptism, had no criminal history, and were in a legal process. An eyewitness said agents did not identify themselves before tackling man and that while coffee spilled, he did not see anyone throw it. Protesters gathered at the airport afterward.
events.micro_summary: ICE arrested a Mexican father and daughter at Seattle airport after one allegedly hurled coffee at officers.
events.summary: Immigration officers arrested a Mexican father and daughter at Seattle-Tacoma airport Saturday while boarding a Los Angeles flight. ICE claimed the woman threw coffee at officers; her lawyer said they were going to a family baptism with no criminal record.

events.extended_summary: More than a million people were forced to flee the violence across the border to Bangladesh in 2017 The UK has sanctioned five senior Myanmar military leaders after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that the country had carried out genocide against the Rohingya minority – marking the first time a state has been found guilty of the crime. A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma. The UK is joined by several other countries, external in acknowledging the ICJ ruling, including Australia, Belgium, Portugal, Spain and Canada. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: "Our response to a crime as profoundly shocking as genocide must reflect our values and must be matched by clear action." events.extended_summary: Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into space Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media outlets. It was not clear which country had authored the reports. Asked about the reports, Rutte said: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the latest reports but dismissed reports citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously". events.extended_summary: In 2026, frontier AI models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic made breakthroughs on hundreds of open mathematical problems. Starting in April with the Erdős unit distance and Jacobian conjectures, progress accelerated in September and October when OpenAI announced a solution to the Navier-Stokes equation, one of seven millennium problems, and released over 700 papers claiming solutions to 372 open problems. Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge announced a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, proposed in 1867. Fields medallist Hugo Duminil-Copin warned the October releases had annihilated his field and could dismantle mathematics. The advances used large language models trained on mathematical literature and AI agents capable of reasoning and executing code; solving Navier-Stokes required 10,000 agents working for 88 hours, plus 17 hours for verification using Lean software.
events.micro_summary: In 2026, AI claimed solutions to 372 open problems including the Riemann Hypothesis and Navier-Stokes equation.
events.summary: In 2026, frontier AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic claimed solutions to 372 open mathematical problems, including the Riemann Hypothesis and Navier-Stokes equation, using thousands of AI agents over 88 hours.

events.extended_summary: Cameron Munster has rejected the Melbourne Storm's latest contract offer, reportedly worth $850,000 per season for one year with an option for a second, describing the terms as disappointing. The 32-year-old Queensland captain declared all options are on the table as he seeks a new home for 2028, though he will remain with Melbourne for the 2027 season on his existing $1.1 million contract, his final year under retiring coach Craig Bellamy. Munster admitted his form was not good enough during last season, suggesting the offer reflected his performance. The rejection comes as Melbourne faces a retention battle on multiple fronts, with teammate Harry Grant meeting Gold Coast officials and receiving an offer to join the Titans, while prop Stefano Utoikamanu has been linked to the Sydney Roosters from 2028. Two Sydney clubs are reportedly interested in signing Munster, who is expected to sign his final contract elsewhere.
events.micro_summary: Cameron Munster rejected the Melbourne Storm's $850,000 contract offer to explore 2028 options.

events.summary: Cameron Munster rejected the Melbourne Storm's revised $850,000 per season offer, declaring all options open for 2028 after labelling the one-year deal with option disappointing. The 32-year-old will complete his $1.1 million 2027 season with the club.

events.extended_summary: Rescuers in Ukraine have raced to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike after attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people. Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly drone and missile barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter while the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year. An overnight strike on Dymer, about 45km (30 miles) north of the Ukrainian capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11 people, Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko said on Monday. “Rescuers recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble,” Tkachenko wrote on Telegram, confirming the death toll had risen to 11. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said earlier on Telegram that the dead included a teenager. It said rescuers were searching for 11 people, including two children, who were “not responding or cannot be reached”.
events.micro_summary: At least 15 killed in Ukraine’s Kyiv region as Russia intensifies attacks.
events.summary: At least 15 killed in Ukraine’s Kyiv region as Russia intensifies attacks.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian marines from the 40th Separate Marine Brigade used uncrewed surface vessels to transport heavy aerial drones across long distances before launching them against Russian rear positions. The Barracuda unit conducted the operation with the "12 Friends of Ocean" unit and the International Legion of Ukraine's Defense Intelligence. Additional uncrewed vessels carried FPV drones to launch points. Operators struck designated targets, reportedly destroying Russian defensive shelters, damaging logistics infrastructure, and inflicting significant personnel losses. Footage showed an unmanned boat carrying a large drone across water before takeoff, followed by drones striking buildings over a populated area. The brigade did not disclose the operation's date, location, or specific equipment types. The full extent of damage has not been independently verified.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian marines used uncrewed boats to launch heavy drones that destroyed Russian shelters and logistics facilities behind enemy lines.
events.summary: Ukrainian marines used uncrewed surface vessels to transport heavy drones deep behind Russian lines, destroying shelters and damaging logistics facilities in a joint operation with allied units.

events.extended_summary: Russia could take several months to a year to remove the collapsed section of the Crimean Bridge following Ukrainian strikes that severely damaged the crossing, Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said during a briefing between President Volodymyr Zelensky and visiting British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting. Ukraine on Nov. 17 carried out a major operation against the bridge, which links Russia to occupied Crimea, bringing down part of its roadway and obstructing shipping through the Kerch Strait. The crossing serves as a critical military supply route for Russian forces in occupied Ukrainian territories. Speaking at the briefing, Zelensky described the strike as a complex, multi-stage operation that also involved destroying Russian weapons used against Ukraine. Zelensky defended the attack as a response to Russia's constant strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. "Not one, not two — 109 attacks," Zelensky said, referring to Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges. "That's why it's an absolutely fair response."
events.micro_summary: Russia may need a year to clear collapsed Crimean Bridge section, Ukraine says.

events.extended_summary: S&P Global Ratings expects India's GDP to grow 7% in both fiscal year 2027 and 2028, positioning the country among the fastest-growing economies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027 alongside Vietnam. Growth during the June and September quarters was driven by strong goods exports, public-sector investment, and household consumption fueled by buoyant credit growth. Export strength is visible in electronics, engineering goods, and chemicals, supported by trade diversification and integration into global supply chains. However, El Nino conditions, uneven monsoon patterns, deficient summer rainfall, lower reservoir levels, and higher input costs threaten agricultural output and push food prices higher. Inflation is projected to average 5.3% in FY27 before easing to 4.7% in FY28, though retail inflation stood at 6.1% in October, above the RBI's 6% tolerance limit. The agency expects the Reserve Bank of India to raise policy rates by 25 basis points in December and again in early 2027.
events.micro_summary: S&P Global projects India's GDP to grow 7% in FY27 and FY28 while expecting RBI rate hikes amid inflation risks.
events.summary: S&P Global Ratings forecasts India's GDP growth at 7% for both FY27 and FY28, keeping it among Asia-Pacific's fastest-growing economies, while predicting inflation averaging 5.3% in FY27 and two RBI rate hikes.

events.extended_summary: Ramayana became the fastest Indian film to cross ₹1,500 crore worldwide, achieving the milestone in 14 days with a gross of ₹1,519.05 crore, including ₹1,009.05 crore from India and ₹510 crore overseas. After 19 days, its worldwide collections reached ₹1,704.65 crore, with domestic net collections at ₹955.45 crore and gross at ₹1,141.65 crore. The film earned ₹196 crore net in its second weekend and became the first Bollywood film to gross over ₹50 crore in each of four South Indian markets. It recorded the biggest worldwide IMAX opening for an Indian film at approximately $6 million and the largest domestic IMAX opening at $2 million. Ramayana also became only the second Bollywood film to exceed $25 million in North America and crossed ₹700 crore net in Hindi, becoming Ranbir Kapoor's highest-grossing film in India by surpassing Animal's ₹553.87 crore net.
events.micro_summary: Ramayana became the fastest Indian film to cross ₹1,500 crore worldwide in just 14 days.
events.summary: Ramayana crossed ₹1,500 crore worldwide in 14 days and ₹1,704.65 crore after 19 days, becoming the fastest Indian film to reach the former milestone and Ranbir Kapoor's highest-grossing film in India with ₹955.45 crore net domestic collections.

events.extended_summary: India's AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, a 96% increase from $822 million in 2025 and the highest nine-month total since 2019. The funding came through 87 rounds, down from 149, with the ten largest rounds raising $1.5 billion or 90% of the total. Neysa raised $600 million in February, Sarvam raised $255 million in June and $90.4 million in August, and Yotta raised $150 million in July. Early-stage funding rose 191% to $1.3 billion despite a 38% drop in rounds to 21, with average round size jumping to $60.2 million from $12.8 million. Globally, AI firms raised $383.5 billion, with India contributing 0.4% and ranking ninth.
events.micro_summary: India's AI firms raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, nearly double last year.
events.summary: India's AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, a 96% increase from 2025 and the highest since 2019, with the ten largest rounds accounting for $1.5 billion.

events.extended_summary: New Zealand pacer Blair Tickner will miss the second ICC World Test Championship Test against India at Hagley Oval in Christchurch due to a right hamstring injury sustained during training in Wellington. Fellow fast bowler Matt Fisher has been called into the 14-player squad to replace him following impressive performances in the recent ODI series against India, where he claimed six wickets at an average of 13.66 with best figures of 3/31, including dismissing Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. The second Test commences Friday, following the first Test in Wellington which ended in a draw after India scored a record-breaking 720 in their first innings. New Zealand are also without injured all-rounder Mitchell Santner, leaving the side short of experienced fast bowlers. The draw in Wellington saw New Zealand relinquish second place in the World Test Championship standings, while India sits fourth with a point percentage of 50.00.
events.micro_summary: New Zealand pacer Blair Tickner misses second Test against India due to hamstring injury, replaced by Matt Fisher.
events.summary: New Zealand pacer Blair Tickner will miss the second Test against India at Christchurch due to a right hamstring injury, with Matt Fisher replacing him in the 14-player squad after taking six wickets in the recent ODI series.

events.extended_summary: India A will take on the United Arab Emirates in their final Group B fixture of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday, November 24, at the University of Doha for Science and Technology Cricket Ground in Doha, Qatar. The match begins at 11:30 AM IST. Following a 48-run defeat against Pakistan A, India A aims to secure a victory to strengthen their chances of qualifying for the semi-finals, as only the top two teams from each group advance to the knockout stage. Led by captain Tilak Varma, the Indian side includes several T20I regulars such as Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. India A previously registered their biggest-ever win by runs scored against Nepal in their first outing. The UAE squad is led by captain Basil Hameed.
events.micro_summary: India A faces UAE in final Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 Group B match after 48-run loss to Pakistan A.

events.extended_summary: Kathmandu: A strong earthquake struck Nepal, with tremors felt across five countries, including India. The earthquake measured 5.3 on the Richter scale. Besides Nepal, tremors were reported in India, Bhutan, Bangladesh and China. The earthquake struck Nepal's Koshi Province on Tuesday morning, with its epicentre near the Lelep area. The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) said the quake occurred at a depth of around 10 km below the Earth's surface. Tremors were reported across parts of eastern and northeastern India, including Bihar, Meghalaya and North Bengal, as well as areas bordering the Himalayan region. Residents of Jalpaiguri in West Bengal were left panicked after experiencing the tremors. No casualties or damage have been reported so far.
events.micro_summary: 5.3 Magnitude Earthquake Hits Nepal, Tremors Felt Across India, Bhutan, China.

events.extended_summary: India announced a $1.62 billion economic assistance package for Nepal to support reconstruction following devastating August floods that killed over 1,300 people and left more than 5,000 missing. Prime Minister Narendra Modi made the announcement after meeting Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah in New Delhi. The floods, triggered by a glacier collapse on August 26 in Rasuwa and Nuwakot regions, caused widespread destruction to roads, bridges, schools, homes and hydropower facilities, reducing electricity generation capacity by around 10 percent. The package includes a $377 million grant for post-disaster reconstruction and a $1.24 billion line of credit for energy projects. The leaders also signed agreements expanding cooperation in education, research, satellite communications and sustainable urban development, and inaugurated a cross-border railway linking Ayodhya in India with Janakpur in Nepal.
events.micro_summary: India announced a $1.62 billion aid package for Nepal after August floods killed thousands.
events.summary: India announced a $1.62 billion economic assistance package for Nepal following devastating August floods that killed over 1,300 people and left more than 5,000 missing, including a $377 million grant and $1.24 billion credit line.

events.extended_summary: India announced a Development Cooperation Package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees to support Nepal's post-flood reconstruction and long-term development after severe August floods caused loss of lives. The package, also described as $1.6 billion, was announced during Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah's first bilateral visit to India since assuming office in March. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences for the victims and stated the aid aims to restore affected families' lives, create opportunities, and strengthen Nepal's disaster response capacity. During the two-day visit, the leaders laid foundation stones for five connectivity and energy projects, signed a joint vision document, and flagged off the Ayodhya-Janakpur Dham cross-border railway line, emphasizing shared cultural and historical ties.
events.micro_summary: India announces 24,000 crore rupee package for Nepal's post-flood reconstruction during PM Shah's first visit.
events.summary: India announced a 24,000 crore Nepali rupee development package for Nepal's flood reconstruction during Prime Minister Balendra Shah's first bilateral visit, alongside laying foundation stones for five projects and flagging off a cross-border railway.
